title: HookConfig
description: The resolved hook configuration the engine receives: hooks keyed by lifecycle point, each entry naming one implementation, what it may change, how long it may take and what its failure means. This is the loader's output, never a file: interpolation is done, script sources are inline, and no member holds a template or a path (ADR 0014). The authored file form is project-config.schema.json. See spec.md §6.

version.description: Configuration document version. 1 is the only value v1 defines; an engine that does not know a version fails the run rather than guessing which members it understands.

hooks.description: Lifecycle point -> the hooks declared at it, in the order they run. A point with no entry is not a point that does nothing: it is a point at which the engine calls nobody.

HookEntry.title: HookEntry
HookEntry.description: One hook at one point. Order within a point is declaration order; each entry sees the changes the entries before it made (spec.md §4.2).

name.description: Identifies this hook in events, in the run's hook report, in errors and in explain output. Unique within its point; a duplicate is hook-config-invalid. A hook that cannot be named in a failure message is a hook nobody can debug (spec.md §6.2).

config.description: The hook's own configuration, handed to it as context.config. Fully interpolated: a component, script, command or endpoint receives values, never templates (ADR 0014). The engine MUST NOT echo these values into events, reports, contracts or logs (spec.md §7.3).

changes.description: Dotted paths into the hook context this entry may replace, e.g. 'parts.request.headers'. The engine applies a change only if it is declared here AND permitted at the point (spec.md §3), and rejects an undeclared change naming the path. For a component hook this narrows the handshake declaration and can never widen it. An entry with no 'changes' cannot change anything, which is what makes an observing hook auditable as one.

timeout-ms.description: Per-invocation deadline. Defaults to 5000 at exchange and state points, 30000 at run points. Expiry is a hook failure, treated by 'on-failure'; the engine bounds every invocation in time, so a hung hook cannot hang a verification (spec.md §5.4).

on-failure.description: What a failed invocation means. Defaults are per point (spec.md §5.2) and are chosen so that the default is never the quiet one: a hook whose failure would make a result misleading fails the exchange.

report-data.description: Whether this hook's 'data' is carried in the verification/hook event and the hook report. Off by default because a hook's scratch is where credentials naturally land; the data still reaches later hooks in the run either way (spec.md §7.3, §10.2).

Run.title: Run
Run.description: The implementation that answers this hook. Exactly one kind; the four kinds are four ways of carrying the same two documents — a context in, a result out (spec.md §8).

kind.description: Which implementation. 'script' is the only kind available in every embedding, because the interpreter compiles with the engine (ADR 0015); the others depend on what the embedding can do and are refused by name when it cannot (spec.md §8.5).

component.description: kind 'component': the name of a declared component implementing the hook interface (design 2.6 §8). The component is invoked through hook/invoke with this context and answers with this result.

source.description: kind 'script': the script's source text, inline. A path is a file the engine would have to read, and the engine reads no files (ADR 0014); the loader reads it, transpiles it if it was TypeScript, and puts the result here.

entry.description: kind 'script': the function the runtime calls, default 'hook'. One script may serve several points and branch on context.point (spec.md §9.2).

command.description: kind 'exec': the executable to spawn. Spawned per invocation, handed the context on stdin, answering with a result on stdout (spec.md §8.3).

args.description: kind 'exec': arguments, passed as given. Not a shell string: an argument vector cannot be re-parsed by a shell that quotes differently than the author expected.

cwd.description: kind 'exec': working directory for the spawned process.

env.description: kind 'exec': the environment the child gets, in full. Deny-by-default like a component's grants (ADR 0013): the child inherits nothing that is not listed here, so a hook cannot pick up an ambient credential the configuration does not show.

url.description: kind 'http': the endpoint the context is POSTed to. This is today's provider-state endpoint, generalised to every point (spec.md §8.4).

headers.description: kind 'http': headers sent with the request, values already interpolated — this is where an Authorization header for a state endpoint lives.

format.description: kind 'http': the body shape. 'janus' is this specification's context document. 'pact-state-change' is the v3/v4 provider-state body ({ state, params, action }) so an existing state-change endpoint keeps working unchanged — the migration case B5 exists for (spec.md §8.4).

When.title: When
When.description: Which occurrences of the point this hook runs at. Members are exact string matches, AND-ed; an absent member matches everything. Deliberately not an expression language — the same refusal variant semantics §3.5 makes for exclusions, for the same reason: a selector that has to be evaluated to be understood cannot be reviewed (spec.md §6.3).

interaction.description: The interaction's description. With states, this is an interaction's identity (contract spec §4.2).

state.description: A provider state's name. At state points this selects which state the hook handles; elsewhere it selects interactions carrying that state.

transport.description: The interaction's transport kind, e.g. 'http', 'message'. Open vocabulary owned by the transport components (design 2.6).
